# Jubilees Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Watchers; Nephilim; The Flood Decreed

---

**5:1** It came to pass, when the children of men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them, that the angels of God saw them in a certain year of this jubilee — that they were beautiful — and they took wives for themselves from among all they chose, and the women bore them sons who were giants.

**5:2** Lawlessness increased on the earth, and all flesh corrupted its way — men and cattle alike, and beasts and birds and everything that walks on the earth. All corrupted their ways and their ordained orders, and they began to devour one another. Lawlessness increased on the earth, and every intention of every human thought was continuously evil.

**5:3** God looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt, and that all flesh had corrupted its way, and that all who were on the earth had done every manner of evil before him.

**5:4** He said he would destroy humanity and all flesh from the face of the earth which he had created.

**5:5** But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.

**5:6** Against the angels whom he had sent upon the earth God was exceedingly angry. He commanded that they be uprooted from all their dominion and ordered us to bind them in the depths of the earth, and there they are bound, kept apart.

**5:7** Against their sons also he was exceedingly angry, for they had killed one another with the sword and had been swallowed up in wickedness.

**5:8** He sent the sword among them so that each would slay his neighbor, and they began to slay one another until they all fell by the sword and were destroyed from the earth.

**5:9** Their fathers witnessed this, and after this they were bound in the depths of the earth forever, until the day of the great condemnation when judgment is executed on all who have corrupted their ways and their works before the LORD.

**5:10** He destroyed all of them from their places, and there was not one left whom he did not judge according to all their wickedness.

**5:11** For all his works he made a new and righteous nature, so that they should not sin in their whole nature forever, but should each be righteous in their kind always.

**5:12** The judgment of all is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets in righteousness — the judgment of all who depart from the path appointed for them to walk in. If they do not walk in it, judgment is written down for every creature and for every kind.

**5:13** There is nothing in heaven or on earth, in light or in darkness, in the depths of the abyss or in the thick darkness — in all the dwelling places — that is not judged and written on the heavenly tablets.

**5:14** And he said: "My spirit shall not abide in humanity forever, for they are flesh; their days shall be one hundred and twenty years."

**5:15** He sent the sword among them so that each would slay his neighbor, and they began to slay one another until all fell by the sword and were destroyed from the earth.

**5:16** Their fathers witnessed this, and after this they were bound in the depths of the earth forever, until the day of the great condemnation, when judgment is executed on all who have corrupted their ways and their works before the LORD.

**5:17** He destroyed all their places, and there was not one of them whom he did not judge according to all their wickedness.

**5:18** For all his works he made a new and righteous nature, so that they should not sin in their whole nature forever, but should each be righteous in their kind always.

**5:19** The judgment of all is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets in righteousness.

**5:20** Noah built an ark in the twenty-seventh jubilee, in the fifth week, in the fifth year thereof.

**5:21** He entered the ark in the sixth year, and shut its doors on the seventeenth day of the second month, in the first year of the twenty-eighth jubilee. The LORD opened seven floodgates of heaven and the mouths of the fountains of the great deep — seven mouths in all.

**5:22** The floodgates poured down water from heaven for forty days and forty nights, and the fountains of the deep also sent up waters, until the whole world was full of water.

**5:23** The waters increased on the face of the earth and covered all the high mountains; everything under the heavens was covered — fifteen cubits above the highest mountains.

**5:24** The ark was lifted up above the earth and moved upon the face of the waters.

**5:25** The water prevailed on the face of the earth for five months — one hundred and fifty days.

**5:26** The ark came to rest on top of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat.

**5:27** In the fourth month the fountains of the great deep were closed and the floodgates of heaven were shut. On the new moon of the seventh month all the mouths of the abysses of the earth were opened and the water began to descend into the deep below.

**5:28** On the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains became visible, and Noah rejoiced.

**5:29** After forty days Noah opened the window of the ark and sent out a raven to see if the waters had receded; but it returned, for the waters still covered the face of all the earth.

**5:30** He waited another seven days and sent out a dove to see if the waters had receded from the face of the earth; but it found no place to set its foot and returned to him.

**5:31** He waited another seven days and sent the dove out again; the dove returned with an olive branch — leaves in its mouth — and Noah knew that the waters had receded from the earth.

**5:32** On the first day of the first month of the year he opened the covering of the ark and looked, and the face of the earth was dry.

**5:33** In the twenty-eighth jubilee Noah opened the ark and sent out from it the beasts and the cattle and the birds and every moving thing.

---
*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows LOGOS throughout. "Lubar" (v.26) preserved as Jubilees-specific toponym. The doublet structure (vv.6-13, 15-19) retained as in the manuscript. "Favor" (v.5) used in accordance with established Gen 6:8 translation tradition.*
